analyst_view.overall: Early view: Fenerbahce (6th) have a new coach in Emre Belozoglu, who replaced Ismail Kartal and started with a 5-0 win at Corum, days after the club beat Liverpool 3-2 in the Champions League. Selcuk Inan's Kocaelispor are level on 19 points, have conceded only nine goals in eleven games and took seven points from their last three, and their chairman called them favourites for this one. Marco Asensio was injured and Archie Brown suspended for the Corum trip, so Fenerbahce's team news needs rechecking.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean lower: Kocaelispor's matches have averaged two goals, their last home game was 0-0 with Rizespor, and Inan's side defends compactly. Fenerbahce are the league's top scorers with 29, but they lost 2-1 at home to Goztepe on 2 November, so goals against an organised defence have not always come easily.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Fenerbahce will have most of the ball against a low block, which tends to produce corners, while Kocaelispor rely on counters and their own set pieces; the split may be more one-sided than 4.9 to 4.6, but the total looks right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards and I lean higher. A big-club visit to Kocaeli usually brings tactical fouls on the break and protests, and Belozoglu was referred to the disciplinary board over remarks about referees in his last weeks at Kasimpasa, so the touchline may be lively too.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots. Kocaelispor's games are low-event and they rarely open up, so I lean lower; Fenerbahce will shoot plenty, but 14 home shots for Kocaelispor look generous for a team that has scored 13 in eleven games.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. With Kocaelispor packing the box and creating little, I lean slightly lower, with most efforts on target likely to come from Mason Greenwood and Irfan Can Kahveci, who shared four goals at Corum.
